neighbours.label: best guess: the subject or verb that opens a new statement about the topic in expository / biographical prose (He was..., The chromosomes are...)
fire: The bishop died in 1820 at the age of eighty. He was buried in the cathedral crypt.
Ravens are found across the northern hemisphere. They are known for their intelligence.
The engineer grew up near the docks of Belfast. He was trained as a shipwright.
Mitochondria produce most of the cell's energy. Their membranes are folded into ridges.
The village school opened in 1872. Its first teacher was a young widow.
Lichens grow on bare rock and tree bark. They are partnerships of fungi and algae.
The composer lost his hearing in middle age. He continued to write symphonies.
The comet returns every seventy-six years. Its tail always points away from the sun.
quiet: The bishop died in 1820 at the age of eighty, and the town mourned for a week.
Ravens are found across the northern hemisphere, from Alaska to Siberia.
The engineer grew up near the docks of Belfast with three younger sisters.
Mitochondria produce most of the cell's energy from sugar and oxygen.
The village school opened in 1872 with only fourteen pupils.
Lichens grow on bare rock and tree bark in almost every climate.
The composer lost his hearing in middle age, after years of illness.
The comet returns every seventy-six years, most recently in 1986.
